subject: Post-demo: Recommended model shortlist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Recommended model shortlist & next steps

Jordan / Priya —

Great to meet you both earlier today. Thanks for walking us through Acme's primary inference goals (customer-facing chat, document summarization, and product search relevancy) and the constraints you called out: average response SLA = 600ms P95, bursty traffic (50-200 RPS), strict PII redaction requirements, and aggressive cost targets for embeddings and generative calls.

As promised, attached is the short list of model variants we recommend for the initial eval, plus the prompt set we used in the demo. High-level rationale below — I focused on the cost / latency / quality tradeoffs so you can map them to your SLOs:  

Recommended shortlist (starter eval):
- Redwood-7B-INT8 (low-cost, fast latency): good for high-throughput chat and embeddings where cost is primary; lower hallucination risk than similarly sized open models due to our tuned instruction profile.
- Redwood-13B-Quant (balanced): ~2–3x quality gain over 7B on summarization tasks at moderate cost; fits your 600ms P95 on dedicated capacity with batching.
- Llama-3-70B-FP16 (high-quality): best for long-context summarization and highest semantic search relevance. Higher cost and latency — recommend as fallback for complex requests or for canarying on a small percent of traffic.

Benchmarks & resources:  
- Eval notebook & raw results: https://drive.redwoodinference.com/drive/folders/acme-eval-notebook (includes prompt sets and scoring rubric)
- Aggregated benchmark report (latency / tokens / cost estimates): https://benchmarks.redwoodinference.com/reports/acme-2026-apr
- Attached: acme-demo-deck.pdf, acme-eval-prompt-set.csv

Next steps I recommend:  
1) You confirm which workloads to include in the eval (chat vs summarization vs search).
2) We provision a 2-week dedicated eval pool (we can isolate data and enable KMS) and seed it with the prompt set.
3) Marcus & Dev will share a short mutual action plan + pricing estimate (attached) and a proposed rollout/traffic-split for canarying Llama-3 rollback policies.

Can we lock in an internal kickoff on Mon 4/13 at 10am PT? If that works we’ll send calendar invites & a short MxP.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

1) For the Redwood-13B-Quant vs Llama-3-70B-FP16 tradeoff, can you share expected P95 latency numbers (when running on Dedicated capacity vs Hosted) for our target 600ms SLA? We want to understand if 13B can meet P95 with reasonable batching or if we need to plan the 70B fallback sooner.

2) For the embeddings use case (search & snippet generation), do you recommend using the same model family or separate optimized embedding models? What are the cost implications?

—Jordan

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Myers <jordan.myers@acmecorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Recommended model shortlist & next steps

Jordan —

Great questions. Short answers first, details below.

1) Expected P95 latency (approx, measured on Dedicated gpu-pool with conservative batching):
- Redwood-7B-INT8: P95 ~ 120–180ms (single-request, low batch); cost: lowest (baseline).
- Redwood-13B-Quant: P95 ~ 280–420ms (depending on seq length & batch); cost: ~2.2x of 7B per-token. Meets 600ms P95 comfortably on Dedicated; Hosted may add network overhead ~50–80ms.
- Llama-3-70B-FP16: P95 ~ 650–1100ms (without large-scale batching); cost: ~6–8x of 13B. For 600ms P95 we recommend routing only critical long-context summarization to 70B and keeping general chat on 13B.

2) Embeddings: we recommend separate optimized embedding models for both quality and cost. Options: Redwood-Embed-2 (low-cost, 1536-d vectors) for high-volume search; Redwood-Embed-4 (higher-d, better semantic coverage) for snippet generation. Using the same family for both generative + embeddings increases latency/cost unnecessarily. Estimated cost: embeddings ~0.2x–0.4x per-call relative to small generation calls depending on dimension.

3) Security / KV cache: Dedicated eval can be configured with customer-managed KMS and we support immediate in-memory-only KV caching (no disk persistence) and optional prefix-stripping to avoid storing PII. Dev will follow up with our security checklist & SOC 2 evidence.

Attached are two quick artifacts: a 1-page latency/cost tradeoff table and a short recommended traffic-split for canarying (suggest start with 95% 13B, 5% 70B for the first week).

Cheers,
Marcus
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

Marissa
